candidate.answerReason: The center distance is 6, and each external tangent segment has length \(\sqrt{6^2-(4-2)^2}=4\sqrt{2}\). The hexagon splits into two trapezoids of area \(12\sqrt{2}\) each.

methods.label: Split the hexagon into trapezoids
methods.explanation:
Join \(O\) to \(P\). This divides the hexagon into trapezoids \(OADP\) and \(OBCP\). Their parallel sides are radii, so finding the tangent lengths will give the trapezoids' heights.

The circles are externally tangent, so their center distance is
\[
OP=2+4=6.
\]
A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent. Thus \(OA\) and \(PD\) are both perpendicular to \(AD\), making them parallel. Also, because \(AD\) is an external tangent, both centers lie on the same side of its line.

Draw \(OH\parallel AD\), meeting \(PD\) at \(H\). Quadrilateral \(OADH\) is a rectangle, so
\[
DH=OA=2,\qquad OH=AD.
\]
Since \(PD=4\), point \(H\) lies between \(P\) and \(D\), with \(PH=4-2=2\). Triangle \(OHP\) is right at \(H\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AD=OH=\sqrt{OP^2-PH^2}
=\sqrt{6^2-2^2}=4\sqrt{2}.
\]
Applying the same construction to tangent \(BC\), with the same center distance and radius difference, gives \(BC=4\sqrt{2}\).

Each trapezoid has parallel sides of lengths \(2\) and \(4\), and height \(4\sqrt{2}\). Their interiors do not overlap, so the hexagon's area is
\[
2\left(\frac{2+4}{2}\cdot4\sqrt{2}\right)
=\boxed{24\sqrt{2}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
